acceptance.migration_domain_index_tests_pass_from_c: PASS - new Alembic revision t4e5f6a7b8c9 (down_revision s3d4e5f6a7b8) verified upgrade/downgrade/upgrade on the dev DB; migration-chain integration test asserts the table, 4 checks, 7 indexes (incl. partial unique + partial watchdog), 3 RESTRICT FKs, and 25 columns after a real upgrade to head; 11 pure lifecycle unit tests cover all transitions, immutability, reuse/force/retry/stale-run and scope rules

implementation_notes: MatchAssessmentModel follows the established version/target model patterns: UUID PK, ForeignKey(ondelete='RESTRICT'), CheckConstraint, partial unique Index with postgresql_where; the DESC-order cursor indexes use postgresql_ops in both the ORM model and the migration for a single source of truth

alembic check reports the known pre-existing baseline diff (legacy tables' created_at modify_nullable) plus a representation diff on the two DESC indexes: reflection returns UnaryExpression columns while postgresql_ops keeps plain columns, so the comparison always differs - the physical DDL is correct and proven by pg_indexes output; documented in the evidence rather than chasing a SQLAlchemy reflection artifact
Complete/fail guards are ordered so the completed-immutability check fires before the status check - a completed snapshot with a score can never be transitioned even by a stale run

The lifecycle module is domain-pure (no SQLAlchemy/Celery/HTTP/LLM imports) and exports through backend/domain/match_assessment/__init__.py; the application worker/API wiring that uses these rules lands in #110
Failure diagnostics are safe by contract: error_code/error_details columns exist for the worker to persist typed codes (ASSESSMENT_*) and short public messages - never provider payloads
residual_risks: The queued/evaluating watchdog index exists but the watchdog sweep itself (stale evaluating rows recovery) is a worker-side concern for #110
Reuse/force/retry application wiring (completed-reuse lookup queries, active-row detection, dispatch-after-commit) lands with the assessment worker and command API in #110
Attempt/run_id ownership enforcement at the SQL layer (optimistic locking) is not yet added; the application worker will enforce it transactionally per RIP-013 7.1/7.2

reviews.note: Version-pinned match_assessments aggregate implemented: UUID PK, RESTRICT FKs, status/score/confidence checks, safe failure fields, immutable completed result columns, DESC cursor indexes, partial active-tuple uniqueness and partial watchdog index; pure domain lifecycle (queued/evaluating/completed/failed transitions, completed immutability, reuse/force/retry/stale-run and scope rules) with 11 unit tests; migration t4e5f6a7b8c9 verified up/down/up and by a migration-chain integration test; 5 schema/constraint integration tests prove partial uniqueness, checks, FK RESTRICT, and immutability at the database layer; full gates green (unit 429/2 pre-existing, integration 120, ruff/mypy 0 new, arch 0 new)
